question: to the Commission Tilly Metz (Verts/ALE), Nicolás González Casares (S&D) Subject:

The Commission’s public consultation on the revision of the Tobacco Products Directive (2014/40/EU) is a key element of the evidence-gathering process supporting future EU tobacco control policy and the objectives of Europe’s Beating Cancer Plan. The ‘Fix the Flaws’ platform1 has deployed a digital tool designed to systematically generate automated, pre-formulated responses to this public consultation. Such campaigns raise broader questions about the distinction between genuine individual participation and coordinated mobilisation efforts designed to amplify specific policy positions. Given the EU’s obligations under Article 5.3 of the World Health Organization (WHO) Framework Convention on Tobacco Control (FCTC), which requires public health policies to be protected from the commercial and other vested interests of the tobacco industry: 1.
How does the Commission assess and account for coordinated or pre-formulated consultation submissions when analysing the results of public consultations?
What safeguards are in place to ensure that organised campaigns do not distort the perceived balance of stakeholder views or undermine the quality of evidence used in impact assessments?

How is the Commission ensuring that its preparations for the future revision of the Tobacco Products Directive remain consistent with the transparency and public health objectives underpinning Article 5.3 WHO FCTC?
https://fixtheflaws.eu/.
